stories.headline: Titletown's Backfield Just Got Blown Wide Open, and the Land Rush Is On
stories.read: Hold up there, pardner, this here's the big one. The league parked Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List after his legal trouble, meanin' he can't practice, can't suit up, and history says fellas who land on that list in early September mostly don't ride again that season. Green Bay didn't wait around neither, they swapped a 2028 sixth to Pittsburgh for Kaleb Johnson to throw in the pot with MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks. Here's your play: Jacobs is a dry well at his old price, but Lloyd is unclaimed territory holdin' a bell-cow's share of the reins in a good offense. Go stake that claim before the saloon sobers up.

stories.headline: Vegas Hands the Reins to Cousins, and Brock Bowers Just Struck a Vein
stories.read: Well now, Klint Kubiak made it official: Kirk Cousins opens under center against Miami, and the No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza starts the year holdin' a clipboard. Don't yawn at that, greenhorn. Cousins has fed tight ends like a chuckwagon cook his whole career, and Bowers is the only real threat in that outfit, which means his cut of the throws is fixin' to be enormous. Healthy knee, veteran arm, no competition for the ball. That's the safest gold on the board at the position, and a rookie quarterback would've cost him three weeks of learnin' curve.

stories.headline: Nabers Won't Promise Week 1, and That Silence Is Worth Money to You
stories.read: Straight talk from the man himself: Malik Nabers ain't committin' to the Dallas opener, sayin' his knee tells him when, not the calendar. He's been off the PUP list and movin' around, but he hasn't taken a full-contact rep and he had a cleanup on that knee to scrape out scar tissue a few weeks back. Now the herd hears wishy-washy and stampedes the other way, which is exactly when you buy. Let some jumpy fella in your outfit push him down two rounds over one missed Sunday, then take a true alpha receiver at a bargain and stash him a week. Diamonds get cheap when folks lose their nerve.
